Dengue Risk for Diabetics Found Higher

A recent study has found that individuals with type 2 diabetes are at a higher risk of developing severe dengue complications. This increased risk is attributed to the body's impaired ability to fight off infections, which can be exacerbated by diabetes. The findings have significant implications for public health, particularly in regions where dengue is prevalent. As the global burden of diabetes and dengue continues to rise, understanding these connections is crucial for developing effective prevention and treatment strategies.
